title: Social Studies Syllabus
text:
STANDARD ONE
THEME: LIVING TOGETHER IN OUR HOME AND SCHOOL
1.0 OUR HOME
1.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) state the meaning of a home
 b) name different types of houses
 c) identify materials used in building houses
 d) identify different parts of a house
 e) state the use of different parts of a house
 f) state the importance of houses
1.2 Content
1.2.1 A home
1.2.2 Types of houses
1.2.3 Materials used in building houses
1.2.4 Parts of a house
1.2.5 Use of different parts of a house
1.2.6 Importance of houses
2.0 SAFETY IN THE HOME
2.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) name different things found in the house
 b) mention the uses of different things in the home
 c) identify things that may be harmful in the home
 d) identify safe methods of handling harmful things in the
 home
 e) state ways of keeping the home clean and safe
 f) appreciate the importance of keeping the home clean
2.2 Content
2.2.1 Things found in the home
2.2.2 Uses of different things in the home
 2.2.3 Things that may be harmful in the home
 2.2.4 Safe methods of handling things that may be harmful in the
 home
 - Fire
 - Medicine
 - Sharp objects
2.2.5 Keeping the home clean and safe
3.0 OUR FAMILY
3.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) state the meaning of a family
 b) name members of a family
 c) mention how family members are related to one another
 d) identify the work done by different members of the family
 e) identify family celebration
3.2 Content
3.2.1 Meaning of a family
3.2.2 Members of a family
3.2.3 How family members are related
3.2.4 Work done by different members of the family
3.2.5 Family celebrations
 - Birthday
 - Wedding
 - Religious celebrations
4.0 OUR FAMILY NEEDS AND CHILD RIGHTS
4.1 Specific Objectives
4.2 Content
4.2.1 Family needs
 - Food
 - Shelter
 - Clothing
4.2.2 Meeting family needs
4.2.3 Maintaining a happy family
4.2.4 Desirable behaviour in the family
4.2.5 Rights of the child
 - Identity
 - Food
 - Clothing
 - Shelter
 - Schooling
 - Medical care
 - Protection
5.0 OUR SCHOOL
5.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) mention the name of their school
 b) identify the symbols of their school
 c) appreciate the importance of the symbols of their school
 d) identify the different people in the school and their roles
 e) identify the roles of members of their class
 f) name the things found in their classroom
 g) draw the seating arrangement of their class
 h) mention their class rules
 i) state ways of keeping their classroom clean
 j) appreciate keeping their class clean
 k) state ways of taking care of things in their classroom
 1) demonstrate the ability of taking care of things in their classroom
 m) recite and sing the first stanza of the National Anthem in
 Kiswahili
5.2 Content
5.2.1 Name of our school
5.2.2 Symbols of our school and their importance
5.2.3 People in our school and their role
5.2.5 Things found in our classroom
5.2.6 Class seating arrangement
5.2.7 Class rules
5.2.8 Roles of members of our class
5.2.9 Ways of keeping tour classroom clean
5.2.10 Taking care of things in our classroom
5.2.11 The National Anthem in Kiswahili (First stanza)
6.0 SAFETY ON THE WAY TO AND FROM SCHOOL
6.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) mention different ways of travelling to school
 b) demonstrate the ability to use the road safely
 c) state the dangers of accompanying and accepting gifts from
 strangers
6.2 Content
6.2.1 Ways of travelling to school
6.2.2 Using the road safely
6.2.3 Dangers of accompanying and accepting gifts from strangers
7.0 IMPORTANT FEATURES ON THE WAY TO SCHOOL
7.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify the main features on the way to school
 b) State the importance of the features found on the way to school
7.2 Content
7.2.1 Features found on the way to school
7.2.2 Importance of features found on the way to school
 STANDARD TWO
THEME: LIVING TOGETHER IN SCHOOL AND
NEIGHBOURHOOD
1.0 OUR SCHOOL AND ITS SURROUNDINGS
1.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) identify buildings in the school
 b) state where the school is found
 c) observe the weather experienced around the school
2.0 Content
2.1.1 Buildings in the school
2.1.2 Location of the school
2.1.3 Weather around the school
3.0 ACTIVITIES IN THE SCHOOL
3.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) appreciate the need to learn
 b) identify the games played in school
 c) state ways of keeping the school compound clean
 d) appreciate keeping the school compound clean
 e) state the school rules
 f) recite and sing the second stanza of the National Anthem in
 Kiswahili
3.2 Content
3.2.1 The need to learn
3.2.2 Games played at school
3.2.3 Ways of keeping the school compound clean
3.2.4 School rules
3.2.5 The National Anthem(second stanza in Kiswahili)
4.0 OUR NEEDS AT SCHOOL
4.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name the items required at school for learning
 b) state his/her needs at school
 c) state ways in which his/her needs at school are met
 d) state the problems faced in trying to meet his/her needs at school
 e) demonstrate ability of caring for things in school
 f) appreciate the need to take care of things in school
4.2 Content
4.2.1 Items required at school for learning
4.2.2 Our needs at school
4.2.3 Ways of meeting our needs at school
4.2.4 Problems faced in meeting our needs at school
4.2.5 Caring for things in school
5.0 SAFE TRAVEL TO AND FROM SCHOOL
5.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name the basic road signs
 b) appreciate the importance of road signs
 c) mention the dangers on the way to and from school
5.2 Content
5.2.1 Basic road signs
 - Pedestrian crossing
 - Traffic lights
 - Children crossing
 - Bends and bumps
5.2.2 Dangers on the way to and from school
 - Dangerous animals, insects and plants
 - Open pits
6.0 OUR SCHOOL COMMUNITY
6.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name pupils in their class
 b) identify the teachers and workers
 c) state the role of pupils in their school
 d) State the role of teachers and workers
6.2 Content
6.2.1 Names of Pupils in the class
6.2.2 teachers and workers in the school
6.2.3 Role of pupils in the school
6.2.4 Role of teachers and workers in the school
7.0 THE SCHOOL NEIGHBOURHOOD
7.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify the main physical features around the school
 b) identify the community groups living around the school
 c) list needs of the people living around the school
 d) state how people around the school meet their needs
 e) state the social activities of the people around the school
7.2 Content
7.2.1 Main Physical features around the school
7.2.2 Communities living around the school
7.2.3 Needs of the people living around the school
7.2.4 Ways in which people around the school meet their needs
7.2.5 Social activities
 - Games and sports
 - Songs and dances
 - Worship
8.0 CHILD PROTECTION
8.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) state the Rights of a Child
 b) identify types of child abuse at home and school
 c) state ways children can be protected from abuse
8.2 Content
8.2.1 Child Rights
8.2.2 Child abuse at home and school
8.2.3 Protecting children from abuse
7. RESOURCES IN THE LOCATION
7.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify the main resources found in the Location
 b) state the importance of the resources found in the Location
 c) name market centres in the location
7.2 Content
7.2.1 The Main resources in the location
 - Crops
 - Animals
 - Fish
 - Honey
7.2.2 Importance of resources in the location
7.2.3 Market centres in the Location
 NB. Teach what is found in the location
10.0 ADMINISTRATION IN THE LOCATION
10.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify the administrative Location where the school is found
 b) mention the administrative units in the Location
 c) outline the order of administrative units in the Location
 d) state the role of administrators in the Location
 e) appreciate the role of administrators in the Location
10.2 Content
10.2.1 Name of the Location where the school is found
10.2.2 Administrative units in the Location
10.2.3 Order of administration in the Location
10.2.4 Role of administrators in the Location
 STANDARD THREE
THEME: LIVING TOGETHER IN THE DISTRICT
1.0 PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT
1.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name the district in which the school is found
 b) name the divisions that make up the district
 c) name the four cardinal points of a compass
 d) use the four compass points to give direction of places
 e) identify the main physical features found in the district
 f) state the importance of physical features in the district
1.2 Content
1.2.1 District where the school is found
1.2.2 Divisions that make up the district
1.2.3 Direction
 - Right and left
 - Cardinal points of a compass
1.2.4 Using the four compass points to give direction
1.2.5 Main physical features in the district
1.2.6 Importance of the main physical features in the district
2.0 WEATHER AND SEASONS IN THE DISTRICT
2.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) list the elements of weather;
 b) state the effects of weather on human activities;
 c) list ways of protecting oneself from bad weather;
 d) name the seasons experienced in the district;
 e) state the activities carried out during each season.
2.2 Content
2.2.1 Elements of weather: rain, sunshine, wind and clouds
2.2.2 Effects of weather on human activities
2.2.3 Ways of protecting oneself from bad weather
2.2.4 Seasons experienced in the district
2.2.5 Activities carried out during different seasons
2. COMMUNITIES LIVING IN THE DISTRICT
2.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify communities living in the district
 b) state different ways in which people in the district depend on one
 another
 c) appreciate the ways in which people depend on one another in the
 district
2.2 Content
2.2.1 Communities living in the district
2.2.2 Interdependence of communities in the district
3. OUR NEEDS IN THE DISTRICT
3.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify the types of needs in the district
 b) state how the needs in the district are met
 c) appreciate the efforts being made to meet our needs in the district
3.2 Content
3.2.1 Types of needs in the district
3.2.2 Meeting the needs in the district
4. RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES
4.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) list resources found in the district
 b) state the importance of resources in the district
 c) state ways in which resources could be used effectively
 d) identify economic activities practiced in the district
 e) state the importance of economic activities in the district
 f) name the urban centres in the district
 g) identify the means of travel in the district
4.2 Content
4.2.1 Resources in the district
4.2.2 Importance of the resources in the district
4.2.3 Effective use of resources
4.2.4 Economic activities in the district
4.2.5 Importance of economic activities in the district
5.4.6 Main urban centres in the district
5.4.7 Means of travel in the district
5. CARING FOR THE ENVIRONMENT
5.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) identify sources of water
 b) mention the uses of water
 c) state how water sources may be protected
 d) state the uses of trees found in the district
 e) state how trees should be cared for
 f) desire to participate in the tree planting activities
 g) name the animals found in the district
 h) state ways of caring for animals
6.2 Content
6.2.1 Sources water
6.2.2 Uses of water
6.2.3 Caring for water sources
6.2.4 Uses of trees
6.2.5 Caring for trees
6.2.6 Animals found in the District
 - Domestic
 - Wild
6.2.7 Caring for animals
6. ADMINISTRATION IN THE DISTRICT
6.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:-
 a) identify the administrative units in the district
 b) outline the order of administration in the district
 c) state the duties of administrative leaders in the district
 d) appreciate the role of administrative leaders in the district
 e) state the importance of maintaining law and order in society
 f) appreciate the importance of maintaining law and order in society
6.2 Content
 1.1 Administrative units in the District
 1.2 Order of administration in the District
 1.3 Duties of administrative leaders in the District
 - District Commissioner
 - District Officer
 1.4 Importance of law and order in society
 STANDARD FOUR
THEME: LIVING TOGETHER IN THE PROVINCE
1.0 PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT
1.1. Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name the Province where the school is located
 b) identify the districts that make up the Province
 c) name the eight points of the compass
 d) use the eight point compass to give direction
 e) identify the main physical features in the Province
 f) state the importance of physical features in the Province
 g) identify the main types of natural vegetation in the Province
 h) state the importance of vegetation in the Province
 i) state the meaning of weather
 j) name weather measuring instruments
1.2 Content
1.2.1 Province where the school is located
1.2.2 Districts making up the Province
1.2.3 Eight points of the compass
1.2.4 Using the eight point compass to give direction
1.2.5 Major physical features in the Province
 • rivers
 • lakes
 • mountains
 • hills
 • plains
 • valleys
1.2.6 Importance of physical features in the Province
1.2.7 Main types of natural Vegetation in the Province
1.2.8 Distribution of natural vegetation in the Province
1.2.9 Importance of vegetation in the Province
1.2.10 Meaning of weather
1.2.11 Weather measuring instruments
 • thermometer
 • wind vane
 • rain gauge
 NB: Teach only the Province in which the school is located
2.0 PEOPLE AND POPULATION
2.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name the language groups found in the Province
 b) identify areas of high population density in the Province
 c) identify areas of low population density in the Province
2.2 Content
2.2.1 Language groups in the Province
 • Bantu
 • Cushites
 • Nilotes
 • Semites
 • Asians
 • Europeans
2.2.2 Areas of high population density in the Province
2.2.3 Areas of low Population density in the Province
3.0 SOCIAL RELATIONS AND CULTURAL ACTIVITIES
3.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify moral values in the society
 b) state the importance of moral values in the society
 c) appreciate the importance of moral values in the society
 d) describe the traditional way of life of the people in the Province
 e) name the ceremonies and festivals held in the Province
 f) appreciate the role of ceremonies and festivals in the society
 g) state the importance of working together in the community
3.2 Content
3.2.1 Moral values in the society
3.2.2 Importance of moral values
3.2.3 Traditional way of life
 - Food
 - dressing
 - Songs and dances
 - Traditional medical practices
3.2.4 Ceremonies and Festivals
 • Ceremonies
 - birth and naming
 - initiation
 • Festivals
 - harvest
 - music
 - drama
3.2.5 Importance of working together in the community
1. RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES
1.1 Agriculture
1.1.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) name the cash crops and food crops grown in the Province
 b) identify the areas where the cash crops are grown
 c) name the types of livestock kept in the Province
1.1.2 Content
1.1.2.1 The main cash crops and food crops
1.1.2.2 Areas where the cash crops are grown
1.1.2.3 Types of livestock kept in the province
NB: details of breeds are not required
4.2 Fishing
4.2.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify areas where fishing is practiced in the Province
 b) state the importance of fishing
4.2 Content
4.2.2.1 Fishing in the Province
4.2.2.2 Importance of Fishing
4.3 Forestry
4.3.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) locate the major forests in the Province
 b) state the importance of forests
4.3.2 Content
4.3.2.1 Distribution of forests in the Province
4.3.2.2 Importance of forests
4.4 Wildlife and Tourism
4.4.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) identify the types wildlife in the Province
 b) name and locate the game parks and reserves in the Province
 c) state the major tourist attractions in the Province
4.4.2 Content
4.4.2.1 Types of Wildlife in the Province
4.4.2.2 Game parks and reserves in the Province
4.4.2.3 Major tourist attractions in the Province
4.5 Industries
4.5.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learners should be able to:
 a) identify traditional industries in the Province
 b) list the products of traditional industries
4.5.2 Content
4.5.2.1 Traditional Industries
4.5.2.2 Products of traditional industries
4.6 Trade
4.6.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) state the meaning of trade
 b) state the methods of trade
 c) name and locate the major trading centres in the Province
4.6.2 Content
4.6.2.1 Meaning of trade
4.62.2 Methods of Trade
 - Barter trade
 - Currency trade
4.6.2.3 Major trading centres in the Province
4.7 Transport and Communication
4.7.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) state the meaning of transport
 b) list the early forms of transport
 c) list the present forms of transport
 d) identify some major road signs
 e) state the meaning of communication
 f) list the early forms of communication
4.7.2 Content
4.7.2.1 Meaning of transport
4.7.2.2. Early forms of transport
4.7.2.3 Present forms of transport
4.7.2.4 Major Road signs
 - Cattle crossing
 - Round about
 - Train crossing
 - Road junction
4.7.2.5 Meaning of communication
4.7.2.6 Early forms of communication
2. CITIZENSHIP
2.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) define the term citizen and citizenship
 b) state qualities of a good citizen
 c) desire to be a good citizen
2.2 Content
2.2.1 Meaning of a citizen and citizenship
2.2.2 Qualities of a good citizen
3. DEMOCRACY AND HUMAN RIGHTS
3.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) state the meaning of the term democracy
 b) state ways in which democracy can be applied in school
 c) state the importance of democracy in school
 d) state the meaning of the term human rights
 e) identify some human rights
3.2 Content
3.2.1 Meaning of democracy
3.2.2 Ways in which democracy can be applied in school
3.2.3 Importance of democracy in school
3.2.4 Meaning of human rights
3.2.5 Human rights
 • Life
 • Fresh air
 • Clean water
 • Balanced diet
 • Safe and clean environment
 • Shelter
 • Clothing
 • Security
 • Expression of opinion
 • Education
 • Right to own property
4. LAW, PEACE AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION
4.1 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) state causes of disagreements in school
 b) identify peaceful ways of resolving disagreements in school
 c) state the importance of peace in the society
 d) state the importance of law and order in the society
4.2 Content
4.2.1 Causes of disagreements in school
4.2.2 Ways of resolving disagreements in school
4.2.3 Importance of peace in society
4.2.4 Importance of law and order in society
5. GOVERNMENT OF KENYA
5.1 Provincial Administration
8.1.0 Specific Objectives
 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
 a) outline the structure of administration in the Province
 b) state the duties of the Provincial Commissioner
 c) appreciate the role of provincial administration
5.2 Content
5.2.1 Structure of Provincial Administration
5.2.2 Duties of the Provincial Commissioner

 By the end of this topic, the learner should be able to:
